S/U Only
Tags: courses
Short Description: A grading method in which student performance is recorded as S (Satisfactory) or U (Unsatisfactory) rather than a letter grade.
S/U Only

Certain courses do not lend themselves to precise grading. For these courses, only S (satisfactory) or U (unsatisfactory) is given to all students enrolled. S/U courses are labeled as such in the course descriptions in this catalog. S/U courses are not counted as courses taken under the Pass-Fail option.
D1 is the only General Education outcome that can be graded using S/U or Letter Grades. All other outcomes must be graded by Letter Grades.

Kuali’s “Rules” Gadget
Kuali’s “Rules” Gadget
How to input Courses Approved for Double Counting in your ABM Specialization form.
Whether you are creating a new ABM, or modifying an existing, you will be asked to input all courses approved for double counting in a “Rules” gadget.

Click Use Rule Categories checkbox
Click + Add Rules
In the blank box next to A, click the drop-down carrot, and select Double-Count.
In the next blank box, click the drop-down carrot, and select minimum number of credits from.
In the next blank box, click the drop-down carrot, and select selected courses.
Enter the total number of double-counted course credits in the Credits box. In the Courses box, list all courses that may be used toward these credits.
If the ABM allows only a certain number of credits from the courses specified, you can end here and move on to the next section of your form.

If you would like to add a statement indicating that other courses may be considered for double-counting with input from an advisor, program director, or other appropriate individual, follow these steps:
Click the plus (+) sign underneath the blue Update Logic button.
You will now see a blank box labeled with the letter B. In this box, click the drop-down carrot, and select Free form text.
Enter the text to accompany the courses selected.
Text Examples:
“Other 400-level ENG courses approved for graduate credit may be chosen in consultation with the program director.”
“Any 500-level CSF course approved by the advisor.”
“Nine credits may be double counted for the ABM Degree. Only 500­-level courses and 400­-level courses designated for graduate credit are eligible to be double counted.”

Topics Course
Tags: courses
Short Description: A course that allows different topics to be offered under the same course number.
Topics Course
Topics courses allow different topics to be offered under the same course number.
8.81.20 Open-ended Course. An Open-ended Course shall be administered by the department which originated it. Initially, an open-ended course shall be proposed and approved in the same manner as other permanent courses (8.81.10). Prior to offering a specific topic the content of the course shall be approved in a department meeting.
8.81.21 After approval of each offering of an open-ended course topic, a copy of the title, subtitle, and description shall be forwarded for schedule authorization to the Office of Enrollment Services via the dean of the college in which the department resides. The dean’s authorization shall ensure that no overlap exists between specific topics and existing courses.

8.81.22 A specific topic within an open-ended course may be offered three times. After three offerings the topic shall be approved through the appropriate channels as either a permanent course or as a permanent topic within an open-ended course and shall be included in the University Catalog.

Level
Tags: programs,specializations
Short Description: The academic level of a curricular offering (undergraduate / graduate / dual)
Level
Level identifies the academic level of a curricular offering.

Undergraduate: Courses numbered 499 and below.
Graduate — Courses numbered 500 and above.

Undergraduate: A program leading to an undergraduate degree or credential, such as a bachelor’s degree, undergraduate certificate, or minor.
Graduate: A program designed for students who have completed a bachelor’s degree and are pursuing graduate or post-baccalaureate study, including master’s degrees, doctoral degrees, graduate certificates, and other post-baccalaureate credentials.

In addition to undergraduate and graduate, proposers may select Dual for programs that provide an accelerated pathway connecting a bachelor's and master's degree, including ABM and 4+1 specializations.
Related toolkit entry: ABM
Related toolkit entry: 4+1
ABM (Accelerated Bachelor to Master's): A pathway that allows students to double-count eligible courses toward both the bachelor's and master's degrees, reducing the time required to complete the master's degree
Kuali: ABM programs are inherited from the master's degree.
4+1: A pathway that allows students to complete both a bachelor's and master's degree in five years. Unlike an ABM, a 4+1 does not include double-counted courses.
Kuali: 4+1s are inherited from the bachelors degree.

New Temporary & Permanent Course Email
Date: October 30, 2026 (2026-10-30)
Tags: Temp Course Email
New Temporary & Permanent Course Email
The New Temporary & Permanent Course Email is distributed to all faculty, deans, and associate and assistant deans on the last weekday of each month. Recipients then have seven days to submit comments to the CASC Chair, GEC Chair, or Dean of the Graduate School regarding any potential or perceived content overlap involving a new temporary or permanent course.
The email serves two purposes:
Provides notice of upcoming Faculty Senate review. Courses included in the email have already been reviewed and approved by their respective College Curriculum Committees and will next be reviewed by the appropriate Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee: CASC, GEC, or Graduate Council.
Provides an opportunity to identify potential content overlap. College Curriculum Committees may review the courses included in the email to identify any potential or perceived overlap with courses offered or proposed by other colleges. Any concerns can then be raised before the courses proceed to Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee review.

Dual Degree
Tags: programs
Short Description: Completion of the requirements for two academic majors leading to two different degrees.
Dual Degree
The completion of the requirements for two academic majors, with each major leading to a different degree. For example, a student may complete one major leading to a B.A. and another leading to a B.S. The student earns two separate degrees, with both majors and degrees recorded on the permanent record and transcript.
